heroCommands.command:
git clone https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI.git
cd ComfyUI
pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: ComfyUI is a node-based app for generating images, video, audio and 3D with open AI models like Stable Diffusion, Flux and Wan. You build a workflow by connecting nodes on a canvas, giving you control over every model, parameter and output.
sixtySeconds.problem: Simple image generators hide the steps behind one prompt box, which limits control. ComfyUI exposes the whole pipeline as a reusable graph and is optimised to run large models on consumer hardware.
whoFor: Artists and designers generating images and video
Visual professionals who need fine control
Developers building generation pipelines with an API
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for maximum control and the broadest open model support. Beginners should start with Comfy Desktop, the recommended installer for Windows and macOS.
requirements: A GPU; the README says big models can run on as little as 4 GB VRAM and 8 GB RAM
For manual installs: Python 3.13 (3.14 works) and a recent PyTorch

overview: Workflows are visual node graphs for image, video, audio, 3D and text generation. ComfyUI natively supports models such as Stable Diffusion 1.5, SDXL, SD3.5, Flux, Qwen Image, Wan 2.1 and 2.2, LTX-Video and Hunyuan3D, with templates in the workflow library.

It runs fully offline by default, re-executes only the parts of a graph that changed, manages VRAM and RAM smartly, and supports LoRAs, ControlNets, inpainting, upscaling and more. Any image or video made with ComfyUI can be dragged back onto the canvas to recover the full workflow, seeds included.

You can install Comfy Desktop, the Windows Portable build, comfy-cli, or install manually after PyTorch. Custom nodes are managed through ComfyUI-Manager. There's also Comfy Cloud, a Developer Platform for API endpoints, and optional paid API nodes for closed models.

troubleshooting.solution: Make sure PyTorch is cu130 or higher.
The README advises removing GGUF nodes and models and using native formats like convrot int8 or w6a8 instead.

troubleshooting.problem: Crashes or errors after adding nodes
troubleshooting.solution: Start with --disable-all-custom-nodes, or temporarily rename the custom_nodes folder.
Remove all command line flags; the README says claimed speed-up flags do the opposite.
